page: Amazon Web Services i7i.2xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM clocked at 6 GHz, supported by 320 MB of L3 cache. For local high-speed I/O, the instance includes a dedicated 1875 GB NVMe SSD. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps and contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread capabilities. Geekbench single-core reaches 2299.0, placing it in the top 10 percent of tested servers, complemented by strong single-threaded data compression throughput of 34.68 GB/sec in gzip. Memory performance is robust, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 25 percent and uncached read bandwidth reaching 62.81 GB/sec. Multi-core performance scales predictably across its 8 vCPUs, yielding average scores in PassMark CPU (15577.33) and stress-ng (8787.14). While CPU-based LLM token generation performs adequately on compact 135M parameter models, larger architectures reveal throughput bottlenecks due to core count constraints and the absence of discrete GPU acceleration.

The inclusion of 1875 GB direct-attached NVMe storage paired with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory creates an efficient density profile for storage-heavy services without the overhead of external EBS attachment. The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides ample caching capacity for transactional systems. The instance is suited for relational databases, NoSQL datastores, caching layers such as Redis, search indexing, and real-time log ingestion systems requiring high local disk throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor at 3.2 GHz, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it integrates a bundled 1875 GB local NVMe SSD and provides 5 Gbps of baseline networking. Compute benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core performance, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and fast single-threaded compression throughput. Multi-core compute and transactional database operations align with mid-range baselines, while memory benchmarks reflect high DDR5 throughput. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale AI inference, but its 8 GB per vCPU density and local NVMe capacity deliver balanced efficiency for operational databases, Redis caching layers, and search indexing workloads.
